items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018

ctx.x: Okay here you are basically on a road trip with a U-Haul trailer behind the car and you’re doing your thing. And I salute you for that. Which sort of brings me to, I want to talk about this music that you play and have played over the years with Sam Rivers and all this. And I don’t know, do you like or tolerate the word “free” as in free jazz? Because a lot of times the musicians who are playing the music aren’t people that named it. Or label it.

That’s true. And I have received, when I was working in the studio I used to be criticized by the studio musicians for that other kind of music that I was involved in you know. Not so much the straight legitimate jazz music and so forth, but the free music that I was — because I got attracted to that very early. And one of the reasons I got attracted to that was because in school, primarily in college, when I started studying percussion with Paul William Price at the University of Illinois, I was introduced to…
You make me tired just thinking about it.
